full_judgment:
Syed Refaat Ahmed J: This divorce suit is being disposed of against the backdrop of a prayer for decree of judicial separation in terms of section 22 of The Divorce Act, 1869 ("the Act"). The suit resulted in a judgment and Order of 16-9-2014 by which, however, a Decree Nisi for dissolution of marriage was issued under section 16 of the Act. That Decree Nisi drew necessarily on the provisions of section 10 of the Act as is wholly contrary in its scope, nature, applicability and prescription to section 22. While section 10 endorses dissolution of marriage at the behest of either party on specific grounds shown, section 22 endorses the possibility of seeking judicial separation short of an absolute dissolution of marriage on limited grounds of adultery, or cruelty, or desertion. It is also contemplated that a decree for judicial separation shall have the effect of a "divorce a mensa et torn". The decree of "divorce a mensa et toro" (from bed and board) remains in itself a largely rare, if not obsolete, form of a divorce order which does not end the marriage but allows parties to reside separately. Under section 22 of the Act a decree of judicial separation has the effect of a "divorce a mensa et toro" by which the marriage bond remains technically unbroken but the parties pray for a legal or judicially sanctioned separation. 

 2. A "divorce a mensa et toro", therefore, rises in the context of a marriage as is just and lawful ab-initio and the law remains otherwise averse to dissolving it but for some supervening cause. Thus, for example, the court may decide it to be improper or impossible for the parties to live together should, for example, instances of intolerable ill temper and adultery be cited. Such a decree entitles the parties, although still married, to live apart without being guilty of desertion. An entitlement also arises in such cases for the wife to be supported by her husband while so living apart. An essential consequence significantly of a decree of judicial separation akin to "a divorce a mensa et toro" is that such a decree does not automatically lead to a divorce. The prospects are therefore, always open for a couple to eventually reconcile. Should, however, reconciliation not be possible, it would be open to the couple to proceed with a dissolution of marriage upon divorce proceedings being initiated under the Act explicitly to that end. 

 3. In the course of this suit proceedings this Court has been given to understand by the parties that the avenue available under section 22 was pursued by the plaintiff Silas Reza S. Adhikaree to obtain a decree of judicial separation under circumstances where no entitlement accrued to him under section 10 of the Act for outright dissolution of marriage. It has been impressed upon this Court by both parties that notwithstanding such formal invocation of a section 22 process the parties are agreed on their marriage having irretrievably broken down meriting otherwise a decree absolute of divorce. 

 4. It is noted that the Decree Nisi of 16-9-2014, as issued by a predecessor presiding Judge, apparently seeks to accommodate such position adopted by the parties anticipating, thereby, a section 16 decree absolute for dissolution of marriage. The Order of 16-9-2014 issuing the Decree Nisi reflects a prima facie satisfaction that even given the concept of an irretrievable breakdown of marriage not being specifically recognized under the Act, and the absence in the facts of aggravated grounds for dissolution of marriage outright as contemplated in section 10, the parties have nevertheless agreed on their inability and unwillingness to continue as a married couple. This, therefore, entitles this Court to deal with the parties' predicament in a manner as justice may demand. That notion of ensuring justice inherent in section 16 of the Act appears to have been the intent behind the Decree Nisi issued by this Court on 16-9-2014. Indeed, the plaintiffs supplementary-affidavit of 2-3-2016 draws on such inherent power of this Court to do real and substantial justice under section 16 and prays additionally for a decree absolute of divorce to be made under section 16 read with section 22 of the Act. 

 8. The initial response of the defendant to the Decree Nisi, as reflected in the counter-affidavit of 9-3-2015, has been to dispute the availability to the Plaintiff of the option of an outright dissolution of marriage. Ms. Samadder has indeed contended she entered into and executed the deed of separation of 2-2-2012 under "compulsion" without, however, elaborating to this court's satisfaction the nature and extent of such compulsion. The counter-affidavit itself read with a further application for alimony and maintenance etc. under sections 37 and 42 of the Act, however, dwell on Ms. Samadder being financially short-changed by an unfavourable financial settlement under the deed of 2012. Citing the plaintiff’s reportedly high earnings in Italy and her own efforts here in Bangladesh to make ends meet as a part-time teacher, the Defendant Gloria Samadder now seeks a judicial intervention for increased alimony for herself and sufficient financial support for her daughter until the latter gets married. It is in that context that an additional alimony of Taka 13,00,000 is sought along with an enhanced child support of Taka 25,000 per month. 

 10. The facts as above noted do indeed paint a picture for this Court of the parties mutually agreeing initially on living separately but always of intent never in fact to reconcile and continue with the marriage at any point in time in the future. A perusal of the deed of 2-12-2012 satisfies this Court of such intent of the parties. There is nothing on record that convinces this Court that the defendant Ms. Samadder may have been induced or somehow being compelled to enter into that mutual agreement of 2-12-2012 against her free will and to the prejudice of her interests. These facts and circumstances evidently convinced this Court on 16-9-2014 to issue a Decree Nisi exceptionally as per the provisions of section 16 of the Act notwithstanding the plaintiff initial filing of this suit under section 22 of the Act. Drawing further upon this Court's explicit authority under section 16 of the Act to ensure that justice is served in the facts and circumstances this Court finds no reason why a decree absolute of divorce may now not ensue. The learned advocate for the plaintiff Mr. Md Solaiman Hossain and that for the defendant Mr. Ashok Kumar Biswas remain in agreement that this should be the most reasonable outcome of these proceedings. That said, and as always has been this Court's primary concern throughout, this Court deems it necessary to invoke its authority under section 37 of the Act to declare this marriage to be dissolved but conditional upon certain beneficial terms recognized in favour of the parties daughter Samantha Hridi Adhikaree. 

 11. Accordingly, it is, hereby, ordered that (a) the plaintiff shall make a monthly payment of Taka 25,000 favouring Samantha Hridi Adhikaree up until such date that she attains the age of majority; and (b) no impediments shall be placed by either parent for Samantha Hridi Adhikaree to gain Italian citizenship should she at any point in time before she reaches the age of 18 request for the same as per "Citizenship Rules on gaining Italian nationality" brought on record under Annexure-'H' of the plaintiffs counter-affidavit dated 13-9-2015. It shall further be incumbent upon the parties to execute a proper instrument to that effect recording the facts of the Decree Nisi of 16-9-2014 and the decree absolute of today's date and recording the terms favouring Samantha Hridi Adhikaree no later than 8 (eight) weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment and order and thereafter to file, jointly or separately, an Affidavit-in-Compliance within 1 (one) week of such execution of a proper instrument. The respondent's application for alimony and maintenance etc. is to be treated as disposed of as hereinabove. 

 12. In view of the above, this Court fined no reason why the Decree Nisi of 16-9-2014 should not be made absolute subject only to the observations and condition in the term above. 

 13. Accordingly, the said Decree Nisi made absolute in the terms above.
